koinonia:verdict/61.koinonia:why: The weakest link limits network capacity, so the minimum return period across subunits is a defensible way to carry it up.

koinonia:verdict/105.koinonia:why: Ordinal score aggregated by max, neither summed nor averaged; source and definition given. The unit-range quibble breaks no declared rule R1–R5.

koinonia:verdict/106.koinonia:why: A mean duration aggregated by a trip-weighted mean breaks no declared rule. The source (HCM 2016) and the definition are both stated. The weighting quibble falls outside R1–R5.

koinonia:verdict/107.koinonia:why: Ordinal level carried by median per R2; source named and definition stated. The BJT mixing is a coherence concern, not a breach of any declared rule R1–R5.

koinonia:verdict/108.koinonia:why: Min is not summing an intensive ratio, nor averaging ordinals or medians; source and definition are given. The first check's objection is a preference, not a declared rule.
